open_points.subject: OwnerFormField destination
open_points.text: whether it belongs to the owner's request itself or to the values the owner gives
open_points.question: Within the request or values, which exact destination does each field fill?
options: Each row names an exact property path
The field name itself is the destination path
All request and values objects are flat and the field name selects a direct member
open_points.default_guess: Treat the field name as a direct member name in the selected request or values object.

witness.initial: The values object has both a top-level `amount` member and a nested `expense.amount` member.
events: The owner submits the field named `amount`.
The owner interface reads the submitted field according to the table.
outcomes: The interface writes the text to `values.amount`.
The interface writes the text to `values.expense.amount`.
witness.observer: The owner and any operation receiving the resulting values

open_points.subject: OwnerFormField query coverage
open_points.text: one field of the owner's pages — what the owner types or picks in a form
open_points.question: Does the owner form table also define fields supplied through page queries, or only fields submitted from forms?
options: Only form controls are covered
Form controls and query fields are covered
Query fields use a separately defined table

witness.initial: An owner page has a query field used to filter records.
events: The owner enters a filter value.
The page sends the value as a query field.
The owner interface processes the request.
outcomes: The query field is interpreted using the owner form table.
The query field is outside the table and is ignored or handled by another unspecified rule.
witness.observer: The owner viewing the filtered page

open_points.subject: OwnerFormField tuple positions
open_points.question: How does a field address one position of a tuple or another repeated or positional value?
options: Rows carry an explicit position
The position is encoded in the field name
Positional and repeated values are forbidden
open_points.default_guess: Encode the position in the field name.

witness.initial: The owner supplies a two-coordinate value.
events: The page presents separate fields for the first and second coordinates.
outcomes: Each row explicitly selects its coordinate position.
The interface infers coordinate positions from an undocumented naming convention.
witness.observer: The owner and the operation receiving the coordinates

open_points.subject: OwnerFormField name uniqueness
open_points.text: Facts: the field's name; whether it belongs to the request or to its values; how its text is read.
open_points.question: Must field names be unique in the table, and what required result applies if two rows have the same name?
options: Names must be unique and a release with duplicates is refused
Duplicate names are allowed when the rows have different destinations
Duplicate names are allowed and a precedence rule selects one row
open_points.default_guess: Require unique names and refuse a release containing duplicates.

witness.initial: The table contains two rows named `status`, one read as text and one read as a closed-list member.
events: The interface looks up the submitted name.
outcomes: The release is invalid because names must be unique.
One of the two rows is selected and its parsing rule is applied.
witness.observer: The owner and the release operator

open_points.subject: Unlisted owner fields
open_points.question: What must happen when the owner interface receives a field for which the table has no row?
options: Ignore the field
Refuse the request
Preserve it as unparsed text
Apply a default parsing rule

witness.initial: The released table has no row named `admin`.
events: The owner interface reads the submission.
outcomes: The interface accepts and propagates `admin` using an inferred default.
witness.observer: The owner and the operation receiving the request

open_points.subject: Text field parsing
open_points.text: how its text is read: as text
open_points.question: When a field is read as text, must its submitted characters be preserved exactly, or are whitespace, empty values, or other forms normalized?
options: Preserve the submitted text exactly
Trim surrounding whitespace
Normalize empty text to absence
Apply a separately specified normalization policy

witness.initial: A text field is present and its submitted value is `  x  `.
events: The interface reads the field as text.
witness.observer: The owner and the operation receiving the value

open_points.subject: Whole-number parsing
open_points.text: how its text is read: as text, as a whole number
open_points.question: Which textual forms count as a whole number, what numeric range and sign are allowed, and what required result occurs for invalid or out-of-range text?
options: Accept only unsigned decimal digits and refuse anything else
Accept signed base-10 integers and refuse malformed or out-of-range values
Use the runtime's integer parser and its range
Treat invalid input as an absent value
open_points.default_guess: Accept unsigned base-10 digits of arbitrary precision and refuse the request for any other form.

witness.initial: A field is declared to be read as a whole number.
outcomes: The request is refused because a whole number cannot be negative.
The value is accepted as the integer -1.

open_points.subject: Yes-or-no parsing
open_points.text: how its text is read: as text, as a whole number, as yes or no
open_points.question: Which spellings and representations produce yes or no, and what required result occurs for any other text?
options: Accept exactly `yes` and `no`
Accept common boolean forms such as `true`, `false`, `1`, `0`, `on`, and absence
Use a closed enumeration defined elsewhere
Refuse unrecognized text
Map unrecognized text to no
open_points.default_guess: Accept exactly `yes` and `no`, case-sensitively, and refuse other text.

witness.initial: A field is declared to be read as yes or no.
outcomes: The interface refuses the request as invalid.

open_points.subject: Closed-list parsing
open_points.text: how its text is read: as text, as a whole number, as yes or no, or as one of a closed list
open_points.question: Which closed list applies to each such field, whether submitted text denotes a member name or value and with what matching rules, and what required result occurs for a nonmember?
options: Each row names a specific enumeration and text matches member values exactly
Each row names a specific enumeration and text matches member names exactly
The field name determines a separately defined closed list
Nonmembers are refused
Nonmembers are treated as absent
open_points.default_guess: Require each row to identify a specific enumeration, match its member values exactly, and refuse nonmembers.

witness.initial: A field named `status` is read as one of a closed list containing a member named `PENDING` whose value is `pending`.
outcomes: The interface accepts the member name and produces `PENDING`.
The interface refuses it because only the value `pending` is accepted.

open_points.subject: OwnerFormField release source
open_points.text: The release: the owner form table the data provider holds.
open_points.question: If generated code reads this release constant, what imported data-provider symbol supplies it?
options: The table is exposed as a named imported constant
The table remains a design fact not read by generated code
A later state defines a generated symbol while preserving this release as its source of truth
open_points.default_guess: Expose it as a named imported `OWNER_FORM_FIELDS` constant.
